description: The Claude detection layer: the invisible technical watermark Anthropic embeds in Claude output, and the five writing-fingerprint patterns detectors are calibrated to find. Confirmed by Anthropic support documentation (2026) and detection research.

technical_watermark.what: Anthropic embeds an invisible statistical mark in Claude-generated text. It is detectable by systems, not visible to readers.
technical_watermark.source: Anthropic support article: How Claude marks AI-generated content
technical_watermark.detection: A detected mark is a signal content was processed by Claude, but is not fully conclusive. Absence of a mark does not prove human authorship.
technical_watermark.implication: De-slopping text changes the fingerprint patterns below but does not remove the technical watermark. The two layers are independent.

fingerprint.name: First-person avoidance
fingerprint.pattern: Impersonal constructions where a human would use I
fingerprint.example: One might argue that the situation is ironic. It could be suggested that priorities reflect cultural assumptions worth interrogating.
fingerprint.tell: Claude defaults to 'one might', 'it could be suggested', 'the reader may notice' even when the task invites personal voice. A trained safety behavior that leaves an impersonality signature. Personal essays without 'I' flag detectors.
fingerprint.fix: Write in first person where the genre calls for it. 'The irony here is hard to miss. I believed in working harder than everyone until my first burnout at 26.'

fingerprint.name: Systematic scope acknowledgement
fingerprint.pattern: Pre-emptive limitation statements at fixed structural positions
fingerprint.example: It's worth noting that this analysis has certain limitations. While this is not an exhaustive treatment of the subject, there are important caveats to consider.
fingerprint.tell: Claude acknowledges limits before the reader questions them, at near-mechanical regularity: the close of analytical sections. Humans acknowledge limits when the argument needs defending, not as ritual.
fingerprint.fix: Delete limitation sentences that are structural, not argumentative. Keep one only if the preceding point genuinely invites challenge.

fingerprint.name: Balanced counterargument inclusion
fingerprint.pattern: Every claim paired with its opposite to appear fair
fingerprint.example: While X offers clear benefits, it also presents challenges that deserve consideration.
fingerprint.tell: Constitutional AI trains Claude to present balanced perspectives. Applied uniformly, it produces the hedging seesaw: claim, counterclaim, hedge, every paragraph. Detectors weight this heavily.
fingerprint.fix: Commit to the claim. Name the real boundary condition once, then stop balancing.

fingerprint.name: Triadic list compulsion
fingerprint.example: There are three key factors to consider. This can be understood through three lenses. The consequences fall into three broad categories.
fingerprint.tell: An RLHF artifact: human evaluators rewarded tidy triads, so Claude structures analysis in threes with statistical abnormality. Humans write two points, or five, or one explored at length.
fingerprint.fix: Break triads where the count is invented. Two points stay two. One point gets a paragraph.

fingerprint.name: Conclusion recycling
fingerprint.pattern: Restate thesis, summarize body, gesture at future implications, in that order
fingerprint.example: In conclusion, this analysis demonstrates that X matters. We examined Y and Z. Future work should explore further implications.
fingerprint.tell: The exact formula teachers and RLHF trainers reward. Human conclusions are messy: new angles, provocative questions, or simply stopping when the argument is complete.
fingerprint.fix: Close on the decision, the number, or the next step. Skip the summary round-up entirely.

fingerprint.name: Paragraph architecture regularity
fingerprint.pattern: Every paragraph: topic sentence, support, transition
fingerprint.example: Each paragraph opens with the point, develops it for three sentences, and ends on a lead-in to the next section.
fingerprint.tell: Claude's paragraphs share internal shape. Human writing varies: some paragraphs front-load the conclusion, others bury the point, some end without a transition.
fingerprint.fix: Vary paragraph openings. Bury the point occasionally. Let some paragraphs end hard.

fingerprint.name: Claude vocabulary cluster
fingerprint.example: delve, nuanced, multifaceted, underscore, encompasses, key takeaway, pivotal, realm, vibrant, tapestry, it's important to note, in conclusion
fingerprint.tell: Claude's preferred terms appear at frequencies dramatically above human writing. Detectors trained on Claude output weight these heavily. A single instance is nothing; six per thousand words is a signal.
fingerprint.fix: Replace with concrete, register-appropriate alternatives. 'Nuanced' becomes the actual distinction; 'encompasses' becomes 'covers' or the thing itself.

notes: These fingerprint patterns describe Claude across Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku tiers. The fingerprint is statistical: presence of one pattern is not evidence; the cluster is the signal.
